- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows upward trend but fails to capture sharp downward spikes in true values (e.g., after 75–80 range).
- Model overreacts to recent high values (e.g., 76+), overshooting into 77+ and failing to correct downward.
- True values exhibit mean reversion toward lower levels after initial spikes, but model holds upward bias.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the window, then catches up.
- Model fails to anticipate sudden drops after high peaks (e.g., 80+ → 70+), often smoothing out volatility.
- Forecast assumes linear continuation of recent trend, ignoring structural breaks or policy-driven volatility.
- Model overestimates the persistence of recent highs, underestimating the probability of sharp corrections.
- True values show stronger downward momentum after 75+ peaks, while model remains flat or slightly rising.
- Model should adjust downward when true values show a 5–10% drop from recent peak, especially if preceded by a spike.
